Hi Sara — thanks for the clear requirements and the diagram, very helpful. Below is a concise, pragmatic assessment and our recommended path. I'll follow up with an operations checklist and a short timeline.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Primary: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for the inference control plane and customer-facing endpoint exposure.
- High-throughput east-west within your VPCs: use Transit Gateway (TGW) + VPC peering or TGW attachments to avoid large egress charges and keep traffic native inside AWS.
- On-prem: establish a redundant site-to-site IPsec (BGP) VPN to the prod VPC; use the VPN as an HA/failover path and for auditability.

Rationale (by dimension):
- Security/isolation: PrivateLink provides the strongest account-level isolation (service endpoint in our account; you create interface ENIs in yours). This minimizes attack surface and aligns with 'no internet-exposed data plane'. PrivateLink endpoints are also friendly for SOC2 evidence (endpoint connection IDs, flow logs).
- Latency / throughput: For low-latency, same-region traffic inside AWS, peering/TGW-attached VPCs are best (no NAT, no extra encapsulation). PrivateLink adds ~1–3ms of overhead typically — acceptable for p95 120ms target — but VPN adds variable latency and jitter. If you have high sustained egress between your prod and analytics VPCs, TGW + peering attachments avoids per-GB interface costs.
- Operational predictability: PrivateLink has predictable per-endpoint hour + per-GB pricing; peering via TGW has predictable attachment fees and native data transfer pricing between accounts in the same region. VPN costs vary with throughput and vendor.
- Scalability & limits: VPC peering is simple but becomes brittle across many accounts/regions (no transitive routing). TGW solves that but requires additional setup. PrivateLink scales well for many consumer VPCs connecting to a single service (Redwood) and avoids route table complexity on the service side.

Tradeoffs and blockers:
- If AurumTech requires extremely high throughput between your prod app and analytics VPCs (multi-Gbps sustained), consider TGW attachments for that east-west flow instead of routing via PrivateLink.
- PrivateLink requires you to create and manage ENIs in your subnets; ensure you have IP capacity in the chosen subnets and permission to create endpoints.
- VPN (on-prem): necessary for your colo; ensure Palo Alto can do BGP over IPsec with MTU tuning. If you need guaranteed SLOs over the colo link, we should discuss a dedicated cross-connect (if feasible) — that is higher cost but lower jitter.

Operational ask from AurumTech (short list):
- AWS account IDs for the two VPCs and at least one CIDR/subnet candidate for interface ENIs.
- Contact info for your netops lead to coordinate VPN parameters (pre-shared keys, BGP ASN, IKE policy) and test windows.
- Decision on whether TGW is acceptable (some orgs require netops approvals for TGW creation).

Next steps / timeline proposal:
- Today: confirm TGW acceptance and provide account IDs + subnet CIDR for ENIs.
- 3 business days: Redwood drafts a runbook + endpoint service (PrivateLink) offer and a TGW attachment proposal for east-west traffic.
- 5–7 business days: coordinate VPN handoff with netops and perform a staged traffic canary to measure p95.

Attachment: I'll add an internal cost sketch and a checklist in the next message. If this direction looks good, we can schedule a 30-min netops-to-netops call tomorrow.

Best,

Hi Sara — circling back with a concrete plan and an ask for approval to proceed. Below is the execution proposal and a short checklist for your team to complete.

Execution proposal (two-track pilot -> production):
1) Pilot (3–7 days):
   - Deploy PrivateLink interface endpoint from AurumTech prod VPC to Redwood's endpoint service.
   - Run a 48h canary (5% production traffic) measuring p95 latency and request success rate.
   - If canary meets p95 and throughput is within limits, continue to (2).

2) Production hardened path (after pilot success):
   - Option A (recommended if high east-west throughput): Attach both AuroraTech VPCs to an AWS Transit Gateway and use TGW attachments for intra-AWS traffic; keep PrivateLink for the Redwood service surface (control plane/ingest).
   - Option B (if budget constraints and modest intra-VPC traffic): continue with PrivateLink for all traffic and monitor. We will provide a monthly cost estimate for both options.
   - For on-prem: set up dual IPsec tunnels (BGP) between your Palo Alto cluster and the prod VPC. Use the VPN as HA/failover and for audit trail reproduction.

Checklist for AurumTech to unblock work:
- Confirm whether TGW creation and cross-account attachments are permitted by AurumTech's networking policy.
- Provide AWS account IDs and one candidate /26 subnet in prod for interface ENIs (we recommend two subnets in different AZs).
- Provide netops contact and a two-hour test window next week for VPN bring-up.
- Confirm whether you want us to include a Terraform snippet to create the endpoint and SGs (we can push as a PR).

Timing: if we get the account IDs and TGW approval today, we can deliver the PrivateLink pilot config and runbook within 3 business days.
